newsitem.title: LATVIA: EBRD buys stake in Latvia's Riga Commercial Bank.
newsitem.headline: EBRD buys stake in Latvia's Riga Commercial Bank.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on Wednesday signed an agreement to buy 23 percent of Latvia's third largest bank, Riga Commercial Bank.
Bank officials said the deal was the largest equity investment in a privately-owned financial institution in Latvia.
"In money terms this is around six million dollars," EBRD vice-president David Hexter told a news conference. "This is new money that will be put into the bank."
Latvia last year suffered one of eastern Europe's worst banking crises, sparked by the closure of its largest bank, Banka Baltiya.
The stake in Riga Commercial Bank comes after the EBRD invested in leading bank Unibanka and smaller bank Zemes Bank.
The EBRD is to buy all the shares in a new issue by the bank for a total 2.7 million lats. Riga Commercial Bank's capital will rise to 11.6 million lats after the issue.

"The entry of these strategic investors into the Latvian banking sector signals that in reality foreign investors' confidence continues to improve, not only in Latvia but also in the banking sector in general and in Riga Commercial Bank in particular," the bank said in a statement.
The bank has also attracted investment from Swedfund and a fund management group, New Century Holdings.
They together bought 41 percent of the bank's capital before the new issue and will hold 55 percent of the enlarged share capital.
Riga Commercial Bank was formed in 1989, one of the first commercial banks in Latvia.
